5
On a planet, a vertically-launched projectile takes 12.5 s to return to its starting position. The
projectile gains a maximum height of 170 m. The planet does not have an atmosphere.
What is the acceleration of free fall on this planet?
A
2.2 m s–2
B
8.7 m s–2
C
27 m s–2
D
54 m s–2

hints: Notice the $12.5\text{ s}$ is the time to go up to $170\text{ m}$ and fall back, so with no atmosphere the motion is symmetric - what is the time to fall from rest at the top?
For the downward half of the flight, initial velocity is zero at maximum height and displacement is $170\text{ m}$ downwards with constant acceleration $g$.
Apply $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ to the fall with $u = 0$, $s = 170\text{ m}$ and your half-time, then rearrange to $g = 2s/t^2$ and check the unit $\text{m s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough: With no atmosphere there is no air resistance, so vertical motion has constant acceleration $g$ downwards and the upward and downward times are equal. Half of $12.5\text{ s}$ is the time of flight each way, so $t_{fall} = 12.5/2 = 6.25\text{ s}$.
Consider only the fall from maximum height. There $u = 0$, $s = 170\text{ m}$ downwards, $a = g$, and $t = 6.25\text{ s}$.
Use $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ with $u = 0$ to get $s = \frac{1}{2}gt^2$. Rearranged, $g = 2s/t^2$.
Substitute values with units: $g = 2 \times 170 / (6.25)^2 = 340 / 39.06$ in $\text{m s}^{-2}$.
Calculate $g \approx 8.70\text{ m s}^{-2}$, about $8.7\text{ m s}^{-2}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: This uses the full $12.5\text{ s}$ as the fall time in $s = \frac{1}{2}gt^2$, giving $g = 2 \times 170 / 12.5^2 \approx 2.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and ignores that $12.5\text{ s}$ is up plus down.

B.explanation: Falling $170\text{ m}$ from rest in $6.25\text{ s}$ gives $g = 2s/t^2 = 340/6.25^2 \approx 8.7\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

C.explanation: This is about three times too large and follows from dividing displacement by time incorrectly, for example $2 \times 170 / 12.5 \approx 27\text{ m s}^{-2}$, without the $t^2$ dependence of accelerated motion.

D.explanation: This uses the half-time $6.25\text{ s}$ but omits the square, giving $2 \times 170 / 6.25 \approx 54\text{ m s}^{-2}$ with wrong units and physics.
